newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan one-month NCD average yield at 6.570 pct.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan one-month NCD average yield at 6.570 pct.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank issued T$3 billion in one-month negotiable certificates of deposit on Saturday at an average yield of 6.570 percent, a central bank official said.
The issue coincides with a renewed bull run in Taiwan's stock market, where the index has pushed to a series of seven-year highs in recent weeks.
On Saturday, the index hit yet another new seven-year high, rising 106.45 points or 1.13 percent to 9,501.08 at the close.

The overnight and short-term money rates soared into double digits in late June as investors diverted holdings into stocks, and have been slowly rising again in the past week to stand well above the central bank's 5.0-5.5 percent target zone.
Some investors had also liquidated their foreign exchange holdings into Taiwan dollars, bolstering the local currency and temporarily halting what had been a slow, steady depreciation.

The central bank has confirmed that it was responding to the liquidity situation by issuing NCDs to soak up funds, but has denied repeatedly that it was acting directly in response to the stock market bull run. -- Taipei newsroom (886-2-5080815)
